rationale: Read the five-voter receipt (execution 14e86faf6ccc4b13af3ee46c65cc08dc, exit 0, test passed): all three comparisons are complete and hold, so the starvation signature reproduces when the follower is one of five voters and the leader keeps a majority of healthy followers - the premise recorded a cached claim at index 102 in term 2 over an installed snapshot at 83 in term 3, and the probe again showed repeated installs at the unchanged snapshot index, the follower's applied index fixed while the cluster frontier advanced, and the claim persisting with its suffix kept. The parent account is therefore updated to record the tested voter counts and to drop the three-voter limitation. To finish the persistence question the same way, the driver is now also run for ten seconds, which a local construction run shows keeps the follower at its snapshot index while the frontier advances from 83 to 123 and one stable leader set holds throughout; that receipt is requested here.

interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: a follower that accepts an InstallSnapshot whose index does not exceed its own cached last log index keeps advertising a log it no longer holds, fails every prev-log check from that leader and accepts no further log entry, while the leader retries the same snapshot; the starvation ends only when a snapshot above the cached claim is published, and it reproduces at three and five voters. Source basis: installSnapshot sets lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (src_install_snapshot_tail); getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (src_get_last_entry, state.go 160-174); the non-monotonic compaction path keeps any suffix above the snapshot index while the monotonic branch deletes the whole store without resetting the claim (src_compaction, snapshot.go 217-279); prev-log verification then misses below the store's first index or mismatches the stale suffix (src_append_prev_check, raft.go 1458-1606); the leader walks nextIndex down one step per rejection (src_replicate_failure, replication.go 240-300) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound, which jumps to SEND_SNAP and, on acceptance, resets nextIndex to snapshotIndex+1 (src_send_snapshot_result, replication.go 352-372). Decided evidence: the settled comparison set (execution b6089b103bbb467199d051f4492e82c8, trimmed probe index 14) with the untrimmed control negative on the same fields (index 29); the monotonic-store variant, where the store was emptied while the claim persisted (execution 20c7c72772474093bd6093a37b84448f, probe index 14); the repair boundary, where driving the leader past the claim of 97 and publishing a snapshot at 98 restored the follower to the frontier (same receipt, probe index 33); and the five-voter repetition (execution 14e86faf6ccc4b13af3ee46c65cc08dc, setup index 0 and probe index 14), where the premise recorded a claim at index 102 in term 2 over a snapshot at 83 in term 3 and the probe again showed repeated installs, the follower's applied index fixed while the frontier advanced, and the claim persisting with its suffix kept. Limits: measured on InmemStore plus FileSnapshotStore and its in-process monotonic wrapper with TrailingLogs=10 against a large control, an idle cluster with one write per 250 ms sample, 3-4 s windows and one induced partition, now repeated at three and five voters; a ten-second persistence run is requested with this update and is currently construction feedback (follower fixed at 83 while the frontier reached 123, restores 5 -> 4883, one stable leader set); the vote-decision consequence of the claim is decided in the child question, the configuration-change and wedge consequences likewise, and the follower's commit index staying 0 through the install path is reported as an advertised-state inconsistency rather than an independent defect.
counterevidence: The untrimmed control accepted no snapshot, repaired the stale suffix with entries and reached the frontier in every run, so a stale suffix alone does not stall replication.
A successful InstallSnapshot refreshes the follower's last contact, so the follower never campaigned: every receipt shows one stable leader set with the follower's term fixed.

The starvation is bounded: with a snapshot published above the claim (97 -> 98) the follower caught up to the frontier, so the claim is starvation while the newest snapshot index stays at or below the claim.
The monotonic-store case stalls with an empty log store, so a surviving on-disk suffix is not required for the defect.
limitations: Store and snapshot implementations are the in-process ones (InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, the monotonic wrapper); a production BoltDB-style store is not available in the captured package.
Windows measured are 3-4 s, with a ten-second persistence run requested here; the frontier advance during a window is bounded by the one write per sample.

The configuration-change and vote consequences are decided in the child question and are not re-measured here; the child's minority bound assumes no configuration change between the orphaned suffix and the snapshot install.

scope.description: The trimmed three-voter case of the established scenario run with a ten-second window instead of three, so persistence of the starvation can be observed over forty samples and roughly forty committed writes on the leader while the follower is left ready to accept the leader's repeated snapshot installs.
assumptions: Fault model unchanged: no message loss inside the injected transport; the induced event is one partition of a single voter, its clean shutdown and restart on the same stores.
Only the observation window differs from the decided three-voter trimmed case; store type, TrailingLogs, write pattern, sampling step and the three assertions are identical.
One write per 250 ms sample is the only client load, so the frontier advance is bounded and the leader takes no automatic snapshots.
Reused facilities: MakeClusterCustom with inmemConfig timings, InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, InmemTransport and MockFSM.
excluded: No production logic was modified; the harness only adds test code.
Automatic snapshotting stays disabled so the leader's snapshot index is controlled by the explicit Snapshot() call.

experiment.prefix: Same driver as the decided trimmed case with the window set to ten seconds: build the cluster with MakeClusterCustom (counting FSM), commit sixty entries, partition the initial leader, fire sixty applies on it so they are appended without a quorum, wait for it to step down, shut it down, wait for one of the remaining voters to be the only stable leader, commit twenty further entries there and force Snapshot(), restart the isolated voter on its original stores with a fresh InmemTransport, reconnect it, emit ca_setup with the tag and premise fields, wait for its applied index to reach the snapshot index, then sample every 250 ms for ten seconds while applying one entry per sample on the leader, emit ca_probe and disconnect the victim before bounded teardown.
experiment.requirement: A follower that reinstalls the leader's snapshot must remain able to accept subsequent log entries from that leader, or its cached log state must not claim entries the snapshot superseded; if it cannot, the starvation must be attributable to the snapshot index relative to its cached claim rather than to a transient condition.

comparisons.description: Ten seconds: the follower's FSM was restored again after the first install, with the leader's snapshot index unchanged across the window.
Ten-second progress predicate: the follower's applied index is still below the cluster frontier after the longer window, so the condition does not resolve on its own.
Ten seconds: the cached claim is still at or beyond the installed snapshot index with a lower term, so the operative state is unchanged at the end of the longer window.

experiment.revision_reason: The voter-count repetition is decided, so the next gap in the same account is the window length: the driver now runs the decided trimmed case for ten seconds, which is the only difference. Scenario, stores, TrailingLogs, write pattern, sampling step and assertions are identical to the three-second case.
